title: Krishan Mohan & Ors vs Electrex (India) Ltd on 25 September, 2007
summary: Consumer seeks compensation for non-payment of maturity amount from sick industrial company through fixed deposits.
principle: Unfair trade practice and sale of defective goods or deficiency in service on the part of the service provider
outcome_detail: Partial refund of Rs. 60,000/- with interest from maturity date to realization date, plus additional compensation for mental agony and harassment.
citation: Krishan Mohan & Ors vs Electrex (India) Ltd on 25 September, 2007, (2007)

title: 199Th Report On Unfair (Procedural And Substantive) Terms In Contract
summary: The Law Commission of India has proposed new laws and guidelines on unfair terms in contracts, including procedural and substantive unfairness.
principle: Procedural and Substantive Unfair Terms
outcome_detail: Refunding the consumer for the disadvantage caused by an unfair term in a contract.
citation: 199Th Report On Unfair (Procedural And Substantive) Terms In Contract

title: S.M. Gavai, vs Asian Alloys Limited on 4 March, 2008
summary: Consumer seeks refund and compensation for non-payment of maturity amount in FDRs.
principle: Consumer Protection Act
outcome_detail: Partial refund of Rs. 10,00,000/- with interest @ 9% from the date of filing of complaint and compensation of Rs. 50,000/- for mental agony and harassment.
citation: S.M. Gavai, vs Asian Alloys Limited on 4 March, 2008, (2008)

title: Svb International vs Harjeet Singh on 26 November, 2007
summary: Consumer seeks refund for defective PC after insurance claim rejected.
principle: Consumer has an independent remedy to seek compensation or refund of goods found defective under the Consumer Protection Act.
outcome_detail: Refund of Rs. 32,000/- with interest @9% p.a., and Rs. 5,000/- towards compensation for mental agony and harassment caused to the respondent.
citation: Svb International vs Harjeet Singh on 26 November, 2007, (2007)

title: Bhavraj Financial Services vs Deepa Thadani, on 6 September, 2006
summary: Consumer complaint regarding a financial service dispute involving pre-mature refund of deposits and interest calculation.
principle: Consumer protection against unfair trade practices
outcome_detail: The appellant is required to pay interest at the agreed rate on the deposited amount up to December 31, 1998, and additional interest for any pre-mature refund payments made in December 1998.
citation: Bhavraj Financial Services vs Deepa Thadani, on 6 September, 2006, (2006)

title: Defective Electronics — Replacement vs Refund
summary: Consumer purchased a laptop that developed recurring hardware faults within the warranty period. The Commission held that when a product fails repeatedly within warranty, the consumer is entitled to a full refund rather than being forced to accept successive repairs.
principle: Repeated failure of a product within the warranty period constitutes a manufacturing defect entitling the consumer to a full refund under Section 2(1)(f) of the Consumer Protection Act.
outcome_detail: Full refund of purchase price plus 9% interest from date of purchase.
citation: Rajesh Kumar v. TechCorp India Pvt. Ltd., NCDRC (2019)

title: E-commerce Non-Delivery — Refund with Compensation
court: Maharashtra State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
summary: An online order was charged to the consumer but never delivered, and the platform refused to refund citing courier issues. The Commission held that the seller and marketplace are jointly liable and ordered a full refund with compensation for mental agony.
principle: Charging a consumer for goods that are never delivered is a clear deficiency of service; the marketplace cannot deflect liability to a third-party courier.
outcome_detail: Full refund plus Rs. 5,000 compensation for mental agony and Rs. 3,000 litigation cost.
citation: Sneha Patil v. QuickShop Online, SCDRC Maharashtra (2021)

title: Misleading Advertisement — Partial Refund
summary: Product advertised with features it did not possess. The Commission found unfair trade practice but, since the product was partially usable, awarded a partial refund proportional to the missing value.
principle: Where a product is partially functional despite misrepresentation, relief is proportionate to the deficiency rather than a full refund.
outcome_detail: Refund of 60% of purchase price.
citation: Consumer Forum v. AdMax Retail, NCDRC (2020)

title: Service Deficiency — Appliance Repair Delay
court: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Delhi
summary: A washing machine under warranty was kept by the service centre for over four months without repair. The Commission held this an unreasonable delay amounting to deficiency of service and ordered replacement with compensation.
principle: Unreasonable delay in honouring a warranty repair obligation is a deficiency of service warranting replacement and compensation.
outcome_detail: Replacement of appliance plus Rs. 8,000 compensation.
citation: Anil Verma v. HomeCare Appliances, DCDRC Delhi (2022)

title: Banking — Unauthorized Transaction Reversal
court: Karnataka State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
summary: Consumer reported an unauthorized debit; the bank delayed reversal beyond RBI's mandated timeline. Relying on the RBI zero-liability circular, the Commission ordered full reversal with interest.
principle: Under the RBI limited-liability framework, a customer who promptly reports an unauthorized electronic transaction bears zero liability and is entitled to full reversal.
outcome_detail: Full reversal of disputed amount plus 12% interest and Rs. 10,000 compensation.
citation: Meera Nair v. National Bank Ltd., SCDRC Karnataka (2021)

title: Automobile — Persistent Manufacturing Defect
summary: A newly purchased car exhibited engine defects despite multiple repairs. The Commission ordered replacement with a new vehicle, holding that consumers should not bear the risk of an inherently defective unit.
principle: A persistent, unrepairable manufacturing defect in a new vehicle entitles the consumer to replacement with a defect-free unit.
outcome_detail: Replacement with new vehicle of same model or full refund at consumer's option.
citation: Vikram Singh v. AutoMakers India, NCDRC (2018)

title: Telecom — Wrongful Billing
court: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Chennai
summary: A telecom operator billed for services never activated. The Commission ordered a refund of the wrongful charges and waiver of disputed dues.
principle: Billing a consumer for services not rendered constitutes both unfair trade practice and deficiency of service.
outcome_detail: Refund of wrongful charges plus waiver of disputed dues and Rs. 4,000 compensation.
citation: Karthik R. v. ConnectTel, DCDRC Chennai (2022)

title: E-commerce — Counterfeit Goods
summary: A branded product purchased online turned out to be counterfeit. The Commission ordered a full refund with punitive compensation, emphasising the marketplace's duty to verify sellers.
principle: Sale of counterfeit goods is an unfair trade practice; marketplaces owe a duty of seller verification and are liable for refund and punitive damages.
outcome_detail: Full refund plus Rs. 15,000 punitive compensation.
citation: Priya Desai v. MegaMart Marketplace, NCDRC (2023)

title: Insurance — Wrongful Claim Repudiation
court: West Bengal State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
summary: A health insurance claim was repudiated on technical grounds not disclosed at the time of sale. The Commission held the repudiation arbitrary and ordered the claim be honoured.
principle: An insurer cannot repudiate a claim on grounds or exclusions that were not clearly disclosed to the insured at the time of contract.
outcome_detail: Full claim amount payable plus 9% interest and Rs. 25,000 compensation.
citation: Subhash Ghosh v. SecureLife Insurance, SCDRC West Bengal (2020)

title: Food Delivery — Health Hazard
court: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Pune
summary: A consumer received contaminated food via a delivery app, resulting in illness. The Commission ordered a refund plus compensation for medical expenses and mental agony.
principle: Delivery of unsafe or contaminated food is a serious deficiency of service; aggregators share liability with restaurants for consumer safety.
outcome_detail: Refund of order value plus Rs. 12,000 toward medical costs and mental agony.
citation: Neha Joshi v. FastBite Delivery, DCDRC Pune (2023)

title: Real Estate — Possession Delay Refund
summary: A builder failed to deliver possession of a flat years past the agreed date. The Commission allowed the buyer to withdraw and ordered a refund of all amounts paid with interest.
principle: A homebuyer cannot be made to wait indefinitely; inordinate delay in possession entitles the buyer to a refund with interest.
outcome_detail: Refund of total amount paid with 10.5% interest from date of each payment.
citation: Arvind Mehta v. SkylineBuilders, NCDRC (2017)

title: Subscription — Auto-renewal Without Consent
court: Delhi State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
summary: A streaming service auto-renewed an annual subscription and charged the consumer without clear consent or reminder. The Commission ordered refund of the renewal charge.
principle: Auto-renewal without clear, informed consent and prior notice is an unfair trade practice; the charge must be refunded.
outcome_detail: Refund of renewal charge plus Rs. 2,000 compensation.
citation: Rohit Sharma v. StreamPlus, SCDRC Delhi (2022)

title: Furniture — Damaged on Delivery
court: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Bengaluru
summary: A consumer received furniture damaged in transit and the seller refused replacement. The Commission ordered replacement or refund at the consumer's option.
principle: The seller bears the risk of transit damage until the goods are accepted by the consumer in sound condition.
outcome_detail: Replacement with undamaged item or full refund at consumer's option plus Rs. 3,500 cost.
citation: Lakshmi Rao v. WoodWorks Online, DCDRC Bengaluru (2021)

title: Travel — Cancelled Flight Refund
summary: An airline cancelled a flight and offered only credit notes instead of refunds. The Commission held that consumers are entitled to a cash refund for cancellations not attributable to them.
principle: On cancellation of a service by the provider, the consumer is entitled to a monetary refund and cannot be forced to accept credit vouchers.
outcome_detail: Full cash refund of ticket price plus Rs. 5,000 compensation.
citation: Deepa Krishnan v. AirVista, NCDRC (2022)

title: Mobile Phone — Refurbished Sold as New
court: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Lucknow
summary: A refurbished phone was sold to the consumer as brand new. The Commission found misrepresentation and ordered a full refund with compensation.
principle: Selling refurbished goods as new is misrepresentation and an unfair trade practice entitling the consumer to a full refund.
outcome_detail: Full refund plus Rs. 7,000 compensation.
citation: Imran Khan v. GadgetBazaar, DCDRC Lucknow (2023)

title: Karnataka Housing Board vs K.A. Nagamani on 6 May, 2019
summary: Consumer dispute over housing scheme allotment and refund of deposit.
principle: Section 21(b) of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986
outcome_detail: The National Commission's order dismissing the Revision Petition was affirmed by this Court.
citation: Karnataka Housing Board vs K.A. Nagamani on 6 May, 2019, (2019)

title: Experion Developers Private Ltd. vs Sushma Ashok Shiroor on 7 April, 2022
summary: Developer fails to deliver apartment within stipulated time, consumer seeks refund and interest.
principle: Consumer Protection Act, 1986
outcome_detail: The Developer is directed to refund the amount of Rs.2,06,41,379/- with interest @ 9% p.a., and an enhanced interest rate of 24% p.a. for a limited period.
citation: Experion Developers Private Ltd. vs Sushma Ashok Shiroor on 7 April, 2022, (2022)

title: Sarvpreet Singh vs The Managingdirector/Prop., ... on 10 March, 2015
summary: Consumer complaint dismissed for non-compliance with time limit and lack of consumer status.
principle: National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission's decision on consumer definition is not binding in other forums.
outcome_detail: The appeal was dismissed, remanded back to the District Forum for a fresh decision based on the evidence presented.
citation: Sarvpreet Singh vs The Managingdirector/Prop., ... on 10 March, 2015, (2015)

title: M/S. T.V. Sundaram Iyengar & Sons Ltd. vs Cnr Consumer Rights Protection Cell & ... on 31 March, 2002
summary: The court decides on who is liable for service in a dispute over car bookings, finding Pal Peugeot Ltd., not Sundaram Motors, responsible.
principle: Consumer protection and liability of dealers vs manufacturers
outcome_detail: Pal Peugeot Ltd. refunded the advance booking amount with interest to each complainant.
citation: M/S. T.V. Sundaram Iyengar & Sons Ltd. vs Cnr Consumer Rights Protection Cell & ... on 31 March, 2002, (2002)

title: M/S Monto Motors Ltd. vs M/S Sri Sai Motors on 10 July, 2013
summary: Petitioner Monto Motors Ltd. seeks reversal of District Forum's order dismissing its appeal against State Commission's dismissal of a consumer complaint regarding security deposit refund.
principle: Consumer protection under the Consumer Protection Act, 1986
outcome_detail: Petitioner agrees to refund Rs. 2 lakhs with interest and compensation for mental anguish and litigation costs.
citation: M/S Monto Motors Ltd. vs M/S Sri Sai Motors on 10 July, 2013, (2013)

title: Mrs. Hardesh Mehta vs Parkwood Developers Pvt.Ltd. And ... on 17 May, 2021
summary: Consumer complaint against developers for non-delivery of flat and unfair contract terms.
principle: Unfair Contract Terms
outcome_detail: Refund of deposit amount with interest, compensation for mental pain and harassment, and litigation expenses.
citation: Mrs. Hardesh Mehta vs Parkwood Developers Pvt.Ltd. And ... on 17 May, 2021, (2021)

title: K A Nagamani vs National Consumer Disputes Redressal ... on 13 November, 2018
summary: The High Court dismisses the petition challenging an order passed by the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission regarding a consumer complaint.
principle: Consumer protection laws do not apply to enforcement proceedings for orders in consumer disputes.
outcome_detail: The NCDRC's order is set aside, and the pending application is also disposed of.
citation: K A Nagamani vs National Consumer Disputes Redressal ... on 13 November, 2018, (2018)

title: Amazon India Through Its India Head vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 28 October, 2021
summary: Amazon India faces dismissal in consumer case over alleged non-delivery of product and fraudulent practices.
principle: Cheating is not an offence under Indian Penal Code unless it involves inducing the victim to part with property for a dishonest intention, without their knowledge.
outcome_detail: The court dismissed the complaint against Amazon India, finding that there was no evidence of fraudulent intent or inducement by the Petitioner (Amazon) to induce Complainant (the buyer) into purchasing the product with a dishonest intention.
citation: Amazon India Through Its India Head vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 28 October, 2021, (2021)

title: Mr. Gurpreet Singh vs M/S Puma Realtors Private Limited on 26 October, 2015
summary: Consumer dispute over a residential plot sale where the developer failed to deliver on time and comply with layout plans.
principle: Misrepresentation and breach of contract
outcome_detail: Complainant is refunded Rs.73,86,223.96 along with compound interest for non-delivery of the plot, and an additional compensation of Rs.2,50,000/- for mental agony and physical harassment.
citation: Mr. Gurpreet Singh vs M/S Puma Realtors Private Limited on 26 October, 2015, (2015)

title: Kannan Krishnan, vs 1. M/S. Mantri Developers Private Ltd., on 27 April, 2017
summary: Complainant sues developer for non-performance of residential project, seeking refund and compensation.
principle: Unfulfilled contractual obligations constitute a breach of contract.
outcome_detail: The Complainant is entitled to a full refund of the amount paid along with interest and compensation for mental anguish and costs.
citation: Kannan Krishnan, vs 1. M/S. Mantri Developers Private Ltd., on 27 April, 2017, (2017)

title: Indira Gandhi Medical College & ... vs Dr. Arun K. Narula & Anr on 29 July, 2015
summary: Students admitted under NRI quota in MBBS course at OP No.1 Medical College, Shimla, were forced to leave due to family circumstances and subsequently filed complaints against the college for refund of fees. The State Commission allowed appeals but dismissed the complaint, leading to revision petitions.
principle: Deficiency in service
outcome_detail: The petitioners are bound to refund the fees collected after filling seats vacated by students who left the course voluntarily.
citation: Indira Gandhi Medical College & ... vs Dr. Arun K. Narula & Anr on 29 July, 2015, (2015)

title: Sri Priyabrata Bhattacharya, Son Of ... vs M.S.Aliens Developers Pvt Ltd, Rep By ... on 29 April, 2016
summary: Consumer complaint against property developer for delayed delivery and non-refund of deposit.
principle: Misrepresentation in advertising can lead to consumer dissatisfaction and financial loss.
outcome_detail: Complainants are entitled to a refund of Rs.21,50,362/- with interest on the remaining amount.
citation: Sri Priyabrata Bhattacharya, Son Of ... vs M.S.Aliens Developers Pvt Ltd, Rep By ... on 29 April, 2016, (2016)

title: 1. Mohan Kumar Dalai, Son Of Sri Tata Rao ... vs M.S.Aliens Developers Pvt Ltd, Company ... on 29 April, 2016
summary: Consumer complaint regarding a housing project's failure to provide required permissions and licenses, leading to non-compliance with the agreement.
principle: Failure to comply with contractual obligations can lead to consumer dissatisfaction and potential legal action.
outcome_detail: The complainants are entitled to a full refund of Rs.18,43,989/- along with interest @24% p.a., as well as compensation for mental anguish and damages totaling Rs.60,000/-.
citation: 1. Mohan Kumar Dalai, Son Of Sri Tata Rao ... vs M.S.Aliens Developers Pvt Ltd, Company ... on 29 April, 2016, (2016)

title: Kaluri Venu Gopal, Son Of Mr.K.V.Rama ... vs 1. M.S.Aliens Developers Pvt Ltd, Rep By ... on 29 April, 2016
summary: Consumer dispute over defective apartment complex construction, leading to delay in possession and failure of promised services.
principle: Misrepresentation
outcome_detail: Complainants were refunded Rs.18,07,294/- along with interest @ 24% p.a. for the period from 29.01.2010 to 30.04.2014.
citation: Kaluri Venu Gopal, Son Of Mr.K.V.Rama ... vs 1. M.S.Aliens Developers Pvt Ltd, Rep By ... on 29 April, 2016, (2016)

title: Mr. Aniruddha Mallick vs Ms. Bratati Chakravarty & Another on 5 January, 2010
summary: Consumer dispute over mortgage-free sale of flat, termination due to lack of permission from cooperative society officials.
principle: Specific Performance Act
outcome_detail: The appeal was dismissed on the grounds that it was not maintainable under the Consumer Protection Act and there was no consumer relationship with the respondent in question.
citation: Mr. Aniruddha Mallick vs Ms. Bratati Chakravarty & Another on 5 January, 2010, (2010)

title: Ram Mangal Sanskrutik Bhavan Through ... vs Aanand Dattatray Koli on 21 August, 2018
summary: Consumer complaint regarding booking of a marriage hall for an Indian couple is partially upheld with refund and compensation.
principle: Consumer protection against unfair trade practices
outcome_detail: Appellant retains 15% of the deposit, while refunding the remaining amount along with interest and litigation costs.
citation: Ram Mangal Sanskrutik Bhavan Through ... vs Aanand Dattatray Koli on 21 August, 2018, (2018)

title: Yogesh vs Dlf Homes Panchkula on 21 April, 2017
summary: Consumer dispute over defective products and services, including refunds and compensation for mental anguish.
principle: Defective Products
outcome_detail: Complainants are entitled to a full refund of Rs.41,64,526.00 along with simple interest @15% per annum from the date of default till actual payment.
citation: Yogesh vs Dlf Homes Panchkula on 21 April, 2017, (2017)

title: Kavita vs The Punjab State Federation Of ... on 12 September, 2019
summary: Consumer complaint regarding delayed possession and interest payment for allotment of flat in cooperative housing complex.
principle: Consumer protection against delay in delivery
outcome_detail: The complaints were dismissed due to the lack of evidence supporting the claims, as evidenced by the absence of documents and affidavits from both parties.
citation: Kavita vs The Punjab State Federation Of ... on 12 September, 2019, (2019)

title: Ashok Kumar Sapra vs Three C Shelters Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. on 16 August, 2022
summary: Three parties failed to deliver possession of apartments allotted under a project launched by Orris Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd., leading to consumer complaints and execution applications.
principle: Consumer protection against non-delivery of property
outcome_detail: The judgment debtors are directed to refund the amounts awarded by the Commission, along with interest at a rate of 9% p.a. from the date of respective deposits till actual payment.
citation: Ashok Kumar Sapra vs Three C Shelters Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. on 16 August, 2022, (2022)

title: Makemytrip Pvt. Ltd vs Sh. Vishal Uppal And Other on 11 March, 2019
summary: Consumer dispute over a ticket booking with Makemytrip and Indigo Airlines resulted in compensation for mental tension and harassment.
principle: Consumer protection against unfair practices
outcome_detail: Partial refund of the price of the ticket amounting to ₹13,033/- along with ₹5,000/- as compensation for mental tension and harassment.
citation: Makemytrip Pvt. Ltd vs Sh. Vishal Uppal And Other on 11 March, 2019, (2019)

title: Vinamra Shyamji Sharma vs Orris Infrastructre Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. on 16 August, 2022
summary: Consumer complaint for non-delivery of apartments in Project Greenopolis.
principle: The Executing Court cannot go behind a decree even if it is erroneous.
outcome_detail: Partial refund of amounts and interest as per the Commission's orders dated 19.08.2019 and 20.07.2020, along with compensation for non-delivery of apartments within six months.
citation: Vinamra Shyamji Sharma vs Orris Infrastructre Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. on 16 August, 2022, (2022)

title: Sanjay Gupta vs Orris Infrastructre Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. on 16 August, 2022
summary: Complainants seek enforcement of a decree for delivery of apartments in Project Greenopolis and compensation.
principle: Execution Court cannot go behind the decree even if it be erroneous, as held by the Supreme Court.
outcome_detail: Partial refund of amounts paid along with interest from the date of respective deposits till actual payment to Complainants/Decree Holders.
citation: Sanjay Gupta vs Orris Infrastructre Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. on 16 August, 2022, (2022)

title: Ravi Agarwal vs Orris Infrastructre Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. on 16 August, 2022
summary: Consumer complaint for delivery of flat and non-payment leading to execution application.
principle: Consumer protection law
outcome_detail: Partial refund of deposits with interest from the date of respective deposits till actual payment.
citation: Ravi Agarwal vs Orris Infrastructre Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. on 16 August, 2022, (2022)

title: Pawan Gupta vs Orris Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. on 16 August, 2022
summary: Consumer complaint regarding non-delivery of apartments under a project launched by Orris Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd., leading to execution and enforcement actions.
principle: The Executing Court cannot go behind the decree even if it be erroneous, as held in Vasudev Dhanjibhai Modi vs. Rajabhai Abdul Rehman (1970) 1 SCC 670 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
outcome_detail: Partial refund of amounts paid and interest on deposits, with additional compensation as awarded by the Commission.
citation: Pawan Gupta vs Orris Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. on 16 August, 2022, (2022)

title: Peeyush Kaushik vs Orris Infrastructre Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. on 16 August, 2022
summary: Consumer complaint for non-delivery of apartments and consequent execution application.
principle: The Executing Court cannot go behind a decree even if it is erroneous.
outcome_detail: Partial refund of deposits with interest at 9% p.a. from the date of respective deposits till actual payment.
citation: Peeyush Kaushik vs Orris Infrastructre Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. on 16 August, 2022, (2022)

title: Manoj Aggarwal & Anr. vs Orris Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. on 16 August, 2022
summary: Consumer complaint regarding non-delivery of apartments due to failure to comply with court orders.
principle: The Executing Court cannot go behind a decree even if it is erroneous, as held by the Supreme Court in Vasudev Dhanjibhai Modi vs. Rajabhai Abdul Rehman (1970) 1 SCC 670.
outcome_detail: Partial refund of amounts paid and interest on those amounts.
citation: Manoj Aggarwal & Anr. vs Orris Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. on 16 August, 2022, (2022)

title: Atma Krishna vs Orris Infrastructure Ltd. & Anr. on 16 August, 2022
summary: Consumer complaint regarding non-delivery of apartments in Project Greenopolis.
principle: The court cannot go behind a decree even if it is erroneous between the parties.
outcome_detail: Partial refund of amounts and interest as ordered by the Commission.
citation: Atma Krishna vs Orris Infrastructure Ltd. & Anr. on 16 August, 2022, (2022)

title: Harjinder Singh vs M/S Manohar Infrastructure & ... on 26 March, 2018
summary: Consumer complaint regarding defective products and service deficiency.
principle: Misrepresentation and breach of warranty.
outcome_detail: Replacement of the product with a new one that is free from defects.
citation: Harjinder Singh vs M/S Manohar Infrastructure & ... on 26 March, 2018, (2018)

title: Sudesh Raghav vs Manohar Infrastructure & Construction ... on 26 March, 2018
summary: Consumer complaint regarding defective products and unauthorized transactions.
principle: Unlawful conduct by a business entity leading to consumer harm.
outcome_detail: Replacement of the defective product with an equivalent one from the same brand.
citation: Sudesh Raghav vs Manohar Infrastructure & Construction ... on 26 March, 2018, (2018)

title: Jindal Drilling And Industries Ltd. vs Indocon Engineers Pvt. Ltd. And Anr. on 8 August, 2005
summary: Consumer protection dispute over a nitrogen generator not meeting promised capacity and performance.
principle: consumer protection
outcome_detail: The defendant is ordered to refund the full amount paid by the plaintiff, along with interest at 24% per annum, but only up to Rs. 69,24,520.
citation: Jindal Drilling And Industries Ltd. vs Indocon Engineers Pvt. Ltd. And Anr. on 8 August, 2005, (2005)

title: Saurabh Gupta & Ors vs Hasti Petro Chemical & Shipting on 13 March, 2014
summary: Consumer dispute over defective forklift trucks leading to delay in supply, replacement required within two months, compensation awarded.
principle: Defective products and services can lead to consumer dissatisfaction and legal action.
outcome_detail: The OPs were directed to replace the alleged defective truck with a new one within a period of two months.
citation: Saurabh Gupta & Ors vs Hasti Petro Chemical & Shipting on 13 March, 2014, (2014)

title: Kuldip Kumar Sharda vs Radio Electronic Emporium on 1 February, 2008
summary: Consumer sues for defective refrigerator replacement and compensation after three years of purchase.
principle: Defective goods should be replaced or the price refunded if not within warranty period.
outcome_detail: Lump sum compensation of Rs. 10,000/- to cover physical discomfort, mental agony, and other sufferings.
citation: Kuldip Kumar Sharda vs Radio Electronic Emporium on 1 February, 2008, (2008)

title: Commissioner Of Sales Tax vs Prem Nath Motors (P) Ltd. on 1 May, 1978
summary: The court determines whether replacement parts under a warranty are taxable.
principle: Warranty does not constitute 'sale' for sales tax purposes.
outcome_detail: The dealer's claim was dismissed as the replacement of parts under the warranty is considered to be part of the original sale and thus not taxable.
citation: Commissioner Of Sales Tax vs Prem Nath Motors (P) Ltd. on 1 May, 1978, (1978)

title: Tata Motors Ltd. vs Manoj Gadi on 17 December, 2008
summary: Consumer sues for replacement and compensation after defective car purchase from Tata Motors.
principle: Manufacturing defect is the responsibility of the manufacturer, not the consumer.
outcome_detail: The appellant will replace the defective vehicle with a new one that meets the same specifications as the original.
citation: Tata Motors Ltd. vs Manoj Gadi on 17 December, 2008, (2008)

title: N.Balraj Hyderabad vs M/S.Agile Phototechnics (I) Pvt. ... on 25 March, 2009
summary: Consumer sues for defective photo equipment and unfair trade practices, complaint dismissed with partial refund.
principle: Defective goods
outcome_detail: Complainant receives a partial refund of Rs.16,95,989/- along with interest at 24% p.a., and compensation for mental anguish totaling Rs.20 lakhs.
citation: N.Balraj Hyderabad vs M/S.Agile Phototechnics (I) Pvt. ... on 25 March, 2009, (2009)

title: Bishan Dass vs M/S Sarvpriya Autos Bye Pass on 9 May, 2012
summary: Consumer sues for replacement or refund after truck's manufacturing defect causes financial loss and inability to move on hilly roads.
principle: Defective goods are considered consumer goods if repair is not carried out within warranty period, even if purchased for commercial purpose.
outcome_detail: The vehicle was replaced with a new one.
citation: Bishan Dass vs M/S Sarvpriya Autos Bye Pass on 9 May, 2012, (2012)

title: Raka T.V. & Furnitures Traders vs Mr. Shaikh Rais Shaikh Rashid on 29 September, 2010
summary: Consumer sues for replacement or refund after TV malfunctioned due to local assembly and lack of warranty.
principle: Manufacturer's liability for manufacturing defects is joint and several, but dealers are not liable unless they show that the vehicle was sold on a principal-to-principal basis.
outcome_detail: The consumer is entitled to replace the TV set or receive a refund of Rs.15,300/- with interest.
citation: Raka T.V. & Furnitures Traders vs Mr. Shaikh Rais Shaikh Rashid on 29 September, 2010, (2010)

title: Krishan Kumar Dhanker vs M/S Hydro Spares & Services, on 23 March, 2007
summary: Consumer sues dealer for defective machine and poor service after it was forcibly stolen.
principle: Consumer protection against defective products and substandard services
outcome_detail: OP No.2 refunds the cost of the machine, OP No.1 pays compensation for mental anguish and harassment, and OP No.3 compensates for wrongful action.
citation: Krishan Kumar Dhanker vs M/S Hydro Spares & Services, on 23 March, 2007, (2007)

title: Haier Appliances (P) Ltd. vs K.N. Chanana on 13 April, 2007
summary: Consumer sues manufacturer for defective washing machine and seeks compensation and replacement.
principle: Consumer protection against faulty goods
outcome_detail: The appellant is directed to refund the cost of the machine, issue a fresh warranty for two years, and pay Rs. 4,000/- as compensation and Rs. 1,000/- as cost of litigation.
citation: Haier Appliances (P) Ltd. vs K.N. Chanana on 13 April, 2007, (2007)

title: Sant Sales, Authorized Dealer, vs Vinay Jain on 22 May, 2024
summary: Consumer complaint against authorized dealer for faulty washing machine and service deficiency.
principle: Consumer protection against defective products and inadequate service
outcome_detail: The consumer is entitled to a full refund of the purchase price of Rs. 23,500/- along with transportation charges.
citation: Sant Sales, Authorized Dealer, vs Vinay Jain on 22 May, 2024, (2024)

title: Whirlpool Of India vs Vinay Jain on 22 May, 2024
summary: Consumer complaint regarding a defective washing machine is dismissed, with the manufacturer required to refund the price and compensate for mental distress.
principle: Defective product liability

principle: A cheque issued as advance/security for a transaction that is cancelled before performance is not drawn against a subsisting legally enforceable debt, so its dishonour does not attract Section 138 -- only civil liability for breach, if any, can arise.
outcome_detail: Section 138 complaint quashed; no criminal liability for dishonour of a cheque issued as advance security for a cancelled order.
citation: M/S Indus Airways Pvt. Ltd. And Ors vs M/S Magnum Aviation Pvt Ltd And Anr on 7 April, 2014

title: Dashrath Rupsingh Rathod vs State Of Maharashtra & Anr on 1 August, 2014
summary: Reference on which court has territorial jurisdiction to try a cheque-dishonour complaint under Section 138.
principle: A Section 138 complaint must be filed only where the drawee bank (the bank on which the cheque was drawn) is situated -- mere presentation of the cheque elsewhere does not confer jurisdiction. (Note: Parliament later added Section 142A in 2015, which lets a complaint be filed where the cheque was delivered for collection -- check current law before relying on this for venue.)
outcome_detail: Clarified filing venue; does not itself decide liability on any specific cheque.
citation: Dashrath Rupsingh Rathod vs State of Maharashtra, (2014) 9 SCC 129

title: Shri Ravindra Kumar Goel vs Shri Joseph Daniel on 27 September, 2011
summary: Plaintiff advanced a friendly loan of Rs. 1,00,000 at 12% annual interest, backed by a loan agreement and a post-dated cheque that was later dishonoured for insufficient funds.
principle: A friendly loan supported by a written loan agreement and a dishonoured cheque is recoverable in full via a summary suit (Order XXXVII CPC) where the defendant fails to raise a genuine triable defence.
outcome_detail: Decreed Rs. 1,07,000 plus 6% p.a. interest (pendente lite and future) and costs, jointly and severally against borrower and guarantor.
citation: Shri Ravindra Kumar Goel vs Shri Joseph Daniel on 27 September, 2011, CS No. 105/2011 (Delhi)

title: Fateh Chand vs Balkishan Das on 15 January, 1963
summary: Seller received Rs. 24,000 as earnest/part payment under a sale agreement; buyer failed to complete the purchase, and the seller sought to forfeit the full amount under a contractual forfeiture clause.
principle: Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act lets a court award only reasonable compensation for a proven breach; a forfeiture clause cannot be enforced as an automatic penalty without regard to actual loss.
outcome_detail: Full forfeiture of the earnest money disallowed; only reasonable compensation for the proven loss could be retained, balance ordered returned.
citation: Fateh Chand vs Balkishan Das, AIR 1963 SC 1405

title: Maula Bux vs Union Of India
summary: Government forfeited security deposits after cancelling supply contracts for breach by the contractor.
principle: Under Section 74, where the loss caused by a breach is capable of being proved, the court must assess reasonable compensation instead of upholding a blanket forfeiture clause; only where loss is genuinely unascertainable may a reasonable security forfeiture stand without further proof.
outcome_detail: Forfeiture clause scaled down to reasonable compensation for proven loss rather than the full deposit.
citation: Maula Bux vs Union of India, AIR 1970 SC 1955

title: Order XXXVII CPC -- Summary Suit Procedure for Recovery of Money
summary: Statutory summary procedure available for suits on a written contract, bill of exchange, or promissory note, allowing quicker recovery of a liquidated money claim.
principle: A claim for recovery of a definite sum due under a written agreement, promissory note, or similar instrument may be recovered swiftly where the debtor cannot show a genuine, triable defence.
outcome_detail: Procedural reference only -- not a specific judgment; supports awarding the full claimed amount where no bona fide defence is raised.
citation: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, Order XXXVII

title: John vs Mammootty on 28 February, 1984
summary: Court dismissed revision, holding decree for damages valid as alternative relief was properly pleaded despite abandonment of specific performance claim.
principle: Decree for damages valid if alternative relief properly pleaded; lack of inherent jurisdiction required for nullity.
outcome_detail: Revision dismissed, decree for damages upheld as valid and enforceable.
citation: John vs Mammootty on 28 February, 1984, (1984)

title: Rajendra Nath Saha vs Saraswati Press Ltd. on 14 August, 1950
summary: Suit for specific performance was amended to claim damages after property was requisitioned by government.
principle: A plaint for specific performance can be amended to claim damages for breach of contract.
outcome_detail: Allowed amendment to convert specific performance claim to damages claim.
citation: Rajendra Nath Saha vs Saraswati Press Ltd. on 14 August, 1950, (1950)

title: Muruga Mudaliar (Deceased) And Ors. vs Subba Reddiar on 3 April, 1950
summary: Suit for damages for breach of lease agreement; unregistered document excluded as evidence.
principle: Unregistered lease agreements affecting immovable property are inadmissible as evidence.
outcome_detail: Suit dismissed due to inadmissible unregistered agreement document.
citation: Muruga Mudaliar (Deceased) And Ors. vs Subba Reddiar on 3 April, 1950, (1950)

title: Niranjan Lal Dalmia vs Union Of India And Ors. on 13 May, 1975
summary: Government withheld payment for goods under a contract dispute, which was deemed a breach of contract, not illegal action.
principle: Breach of contract by government is not illegal action warranting writ petition; ordinary remedies apply.
outcome_detail: Writ petition dismissed as non-payment is a breach of contract.
citation: Niranjan Lal Dalmia vs Union Of India And Ors. on 13 May, 1975, (1975)

title: Lotus Logistics And Developers Pvt Ltd vs Evertop Apartments Cooperative ... on 13 January, 2026
summary: Court upheld arbitral award directing developer to amend building plans, pay Rs.128.98 crore damages, and provide compensation for redevelopment delays.
principle: Arbitral awards can be modified for time extensions but upheld in substance unless contrary to law.
outcome_detail: Payment of Rs.128.98 crore damages and compensation for delayed redevelopment upheld.
citation: Lotus Logistics And Developers Pvt Ltd vs Evertop Apartments Cooperative ... on 13 January, 2026, (2026)

title: M/S S.S. Agro Bio-Tech Flour Mills ... vs Arvind Singh on 4 October, 2024
summary: Commercial appeal challenging decree for Rs. 89.75 lakh payment in property dispute between individuals and bank.
principle: Liability for contractual damages confined to individual guarantor when firm not sued.
outcome_detail: Defendant No. 3 ordered to pay Rs. 69.75 lakh; liability of Defendants 1 and 2 set aside.
citation: M/S S.S. Agro Bio-Tech Flour Mills ... vs Arvind Singh on 4 October, 2024, (2024)

title: Balraj vs Nathuram Sharma & Ors. on 3 October, 2023
summary: Petitioner sought to set aside an order rejecting a plaint. The court allowed the revision petition, set aside the order, and rejected the plaint for being based on inadmissible documents.
principle: A plaint must be rejected if it relies on inadmissible documents and fails to disclose a cause of action under Order VII Rule 11 CPC.
outcome_detail: The plaint of the respondent is rejected and the civil suit is dismissed.
citation: Balraj vs Nathuram Sharma & Ors. on 3 October, 2023, (2023)

title: Kasthuri vs R.Hemalatha
summary: Plaintiff challenged the trial court's refusal to admit an unregistered sale agreement as evidence in a specific performance suit.
principle: An unregistered agreement for sale is admissible as evidence in a suit for specific performance.
outcome_detail: Civil revision petition allowed, setting aside the lower court's order.
citation: Kasthuri vs R.Hemalatha

title: Executive Committee Of Vaish Degree ... vs Lakshmi Narain And Ors on 12 December, 1975
summary: College management's termination of principal's service without university vice-chancellor approval was void, but court awarded compensation instead of reinstatement to avoid crippling the institution.
principle: A body governed by statute is not necessarily a statutory body; termination without required approval is void.
outcome_detail: Rs. 21,100 awarded as compensation instead of reinstatement.
citation: Executive Committee Of Vaish Degree ... vs Lakshmi Narain And Ors on 12 December, 1975, (1975)

title: Jagdish Singh vs Natthu Singh on 25 November, 1991
summary: Suit for specific performance of land sale agreement was modified to compensation due to property acquisition by state.
principle: Court can award compensation in lieu of specific performance when contract becomes impossible without plaintiff's fault.
outcome_detail: Compensation awarded in lieu of specific performance for acquired property.
citation: Jagdish Singh vs Natthu Singh on 25 November, 1991, (1991)

title: Life Insurance Corporation Of India vs Sanjeev Builders Private Limited on 1 September, 2022
summary: Supreme Court dismissed appeal by LIC against High Court order allowing amendment to increase damages claim in specific performance suit.
principle: Courts may allow amendment to enhance damages claim if it does not change cause of action and doesn't cause irreparable prejudice.
outcome_detail: Appeal dismissed, High Court order allowing amendment affirmed
citation: Life Insurance Corporation Of India vs Sanjeev Builders Private Limited on 1 September, 2022, (2022)

title: Sirsi Municipality By Its President ... vs Cecelia Kom Francis Tellis on 18 January, 1973
summary: Employee dismissed by municipality without following mandatory rules of natural justice and statutory procedure.
principle: Statutory authorities must follow mandatory procedural rules and natural justice in employee dismissals.
outcome_detail: Declaration that dismissal was void and illegal.
citation: Sirsi Municipality By Its President ... vs Cecelia Kom Francis Tellis on 18 January, 1973, (1973)

title: Ardeshir H. Mama vs Flora Sassoon on 21 May, 1928
summary: Plaintiff sought specific performance of a property contract, later switched to damages. Appeal dismissed as no contract existed.
principle: Plaintiff's renunciation of specific performance bars damages claim.
outcome_detail: Appeal dismissed, no contract found to exist.
citation: Ardeshir H. Mama vs Flora Sassoon on 21 May, 1928, (1928)

title: Rajesh Bhardwaj vs Union Of India & 2 Ors. on 20 November, 2018
summary: Writ petitions challenged termination from service by a joint venture company. Court dismissed petitions, holding no relief available for contractual employment termination.
principle: No reinstatement relief for contractual employment; only damages available for wrongful termination by non-statutory bodies.
outcome_detail: Petitions dismissed, no relief granted as termination governed by simple contract of employment.
citation: Rajesh Bhardwaj vs Union Of India & 2 Ors. on 20 November, 2018, (2018)

title: I.N. Subba Reddy vs Andhra University & Ors on 5 April, 1976
summary: University professor challenged service termination as punishment without due process; Supreme Court held it was valid termination simpliciter under contract terms.
principle: Termination of service simpliciter under contract terms is distinct from punitive dismissal requiring statutory procedure.
outcome_detail: Appeal dismissed; university's termination upheld as contractual.
citation: I.N. Subba Reddy vs Andhra University & Ors on 5 April, 1976, (1976)

title: Hatimbhai Hassanally vs Framroz Eduljee Dinshaw on 31 January, 1927
summary: Suit to enforce mortgage by sale is not a 'suit for land' for jurisdiction purposes.
principle: A suit for mortgage enforcement is not a suit for land under Letters Patent.
outcome_detail: Appeal dismissed as suit maintainable under Clause 12.
citation: Hatimbhai Hassanally vs Framroz Eduljee Dinshaw on 31 January, 1927, (1927)

title: Food Corporation Of India & Ors vs M/S.Babulal Agrawal on 5 January, 2004
summary: FCI appealed against High Court reducing damages by 6%; Supreme Court restored original decree for breach of contract over plinth lease.
principle: Damages for contract breach cannot be reduced arbitrarily without logical reason; High Court's modification without cogent reason is liable to be set aside.
outcome_detail: Trial Court decree for total damages of Rs.17,32,709/- restored with interest.
citation: Food Corporation Of India & Ors vs M/S.Babulal Agrawal on 5 January, 2004, (2004)

title: M/S. Virgo Industries (Engineers) Pvt ... vs M/S. Venturetech Solutions Pvt Ltd on 19 June, 2020
summary: Appeals allowed against orders permitting amendment to include specific performance in land sale suits.
principle: Amendment seeking specific performance in land sale agreements classifies suit as 'suit for land'.
outcome_detail: Orders allowing amendment set aside; appeals allowed.
citation: M/S. Virgo Industries (Engineers) Pvt ... vs M/S. Venturetech Solutions Pvt Ltd on 19 June, 2020, (2020)

title: M/S Hotz Industries Pvt. Ltd. vs Dr. Ravi Singh (Since Deceased Through ... on 28 February, 2018
summary: Suit for specific performance of property sale agreement dismissed; monetary decree for partial refund granted against defendants.
principle: Specific performance discretionary; monetary relief awarded where property dispute exists.
outcome_detail: Money decree passed for Rs.18.50 lacs against D1 and Rs.6.17 lacs each against D2 and D3.
citation: M/S Hotz Industries Pvt. Ltd. vs Dr. Ravi Singh (Since Deceased Through ... on 28 February, 2018, (2018)

title: Arun Kumar Bhadoria vs State Of Uttarakhand And Others on 15 May, 2018
summary: Writ petition sought improved service conditions for Uttarakhand police force. Court issued directions for working hours, pay, welfare, and infrastructure.
principle: State must ensure humane working conditions and welfare measures for police personnel as a fundamental right.
outcome_detail: Petition disposed with mandatory directions for police reforms.
citation: Arun Kumar Bhadoria vs State Of Uttarakhand And Others on 15 May, 2018, (2018)

title: Tata Sons Private Limited vs Union Of India Through The Ministry Of ... on 30 April, 2026
summary: Tata Sons challenged GST demand on arbitral award payments, court found jurisdictional issue and allowed petition.
principle: Jurisdictional authority is prerequisite for tax notice; absence precludes alternate remedy requirement.
outcome_detail: Writ petition allowed, demand quashed due to lack of jurisdiction.
citation: Tata Sons Private Limited vs Union Of India Through The Ministry Of ... on 30 April, 2026, (2026)

title: Siel Limited vs The Punjab State Electricity ... on 26 May, 2006
summary: Industrial consumers appealed electricity tariff orders; appellate court partially allowed appeals and dismissed others, modifying tariff determination procedures and expenses.
principle: Tariff determination power exists independently of prior regulation framing under the Electricity Act.
outcome_detail: Appeals partially allowed with modifications to tariff and expense disallowances.
citation: Siel Limited vs The Punjab State Electricity ... on 26 May, 2006, (2006)

title: Hasvantbhai Chhanubhai Dalal vs Adesinh Mansinh Raval on 12 April, 2019
summary: Plaintiff sought specific performance of a land sale agreement but was denied due to invalid agreement under the Tenancy Act. Court ordered refund of paid amount with interest.
principle: Specific performance cannot be granted for an invalid agreement of sale under Section 43 of the Tenancy Act.
outcome_detail: Refund of Rs. 18,30,000 with 8% simple interest within two months.
citation: Hasvantbhai Chhanubhai Dalal vs Adesinh Mansinh Raval on 12 April, 2019, (2019)

title: Jer Rutton Kavasmanek & Anr vs Gharda Chemicals Ltd. & Ors on 14 June, 2011
summary: Company appeal dismissed as appellants failed to establish case on questions of law regarding share transferability and status of private company under Companies Act.
principle: Section 111A does not apply to private companies that became public companies under section 43A; repeal of section 43A does not affect company's status.
outcome_detail: Appeal dismissed without costs, interim order continued for six weeks.
citation: Jer Rutton Kavasmanek & Anr vs Gharda Chemicals Ltd. & Ors on 14 June, 2011, (2011)

title: Oil & Natural Gas Corporation Ltd vs Saw Pipes Ltd on 17 April, 2003
summary: Supreme Court held that courts can set aside arbitral awards that are patently illegal or in contravention of substantive law, not just those conflicting with public policy.
principle: Court's jurisdiction under Section 34 extends to awards that are patently illegal or violate substantive law.
outcome_detail: Arbitral award directing refund was set aside as it was against contract terms.
citation: Oil & Natural Gas Corporation Ltd vs Saw Pipes Ltd on 17 April, 2003, (2003)

title: Pioneer Urban Land And Infrastructure ... vs Union Of India on 9 August, 2019
summary: Supreme Court upheld RERA amendments and directed states to establish regulatory authorities within three months.
principle: RERA amendments constitutionally valid; allottees fall under Code's residuary provisions.
outcome_detail: Writ petitions disposed; stay orders continued until NCLT decision.
citation: Pioneer Urban Land And Infrastructure ... vs Union Of India on 9 August, 2019, (2019)

title: M.C. Luthra vs Ashok Kumar Khanna on 27 February, 2018
summary: Appeal over forfeiture of earnest money in property sale dispute; court reduced forfeiture to nominal sum.
principle: Forfeiture of earnest money must be reasonable and proportionate to actual loss.
outcome_detail: Defendant entitled to forfeit Rs.50,000; plaintiff awarded Rs.8.50 lacs with interest.
citation: M.C. Luthra vs Ashok Kumar Khanna on 27 February, 2018, (2018)

title: Sri Tarsem Singh vs Sri Sukhminder Singh on 2 February, 1998
summary: Supreme Court upheld refund of earnest money after finding agreement void due to mutual mistake on land area and price.
principle: Agreement void due to mutual mistake requires refund of money advanced under Section 65 of Contract Act.
outcome_detail: Refund of earnest money awarded
citation: Sri Tarsem Singh vs Sri Sukhminder Singh on 2 February, 1998, (1998)

title: Oberoi Constructions Private Limited A ... vs State Of Maharashtra And Ors. Etc. Etc. on 24 March, 2008
summary: Real estate developers challenged notices declaring their purchased land as 'private forest', claiming illegal action and financial loss. The court dismissed the petitions.
principle: Notices issued under Section 35(3) of the Indian Forest Act, 1927, are valid and vest land in the state, regardless of delay or transfer.
outcome_detail: Writ petitions challenging notices were dismissed.
citation: Oberoi Constructions Private Limited A ... vs State Of Maharashtra And Ors. Etc. Etc. on 24 March, 2008, (2008)

title: Tarun Bhargava vs State Of Haryana And Anr. on 29 May, 2002
summary: Court dismissed petition to quash FIR, holding that forcible repossession of vehicle under a loan agreement constitutes an offence.
principle: A loan agreement cannot authorize forcible repossession without court intervention; such clauses are void.
outcome_detail: Petitioner must seek court enforcement for repossession; FIR proceedings continue.
citation: Tarun Bhargava vs State Of Haryana And Anr. on 29 May, 2002, (2002)

title: Neeta Agarwal vs R.L. Gupta on 31 August, 2001
summary: Civil revision petition against an unconditional leave to defend in a money recovery suit based on dishonoured cheques.
principle: Leave to defend in summary suits requires a real defense, not a sham, and conditional security may be imposed.
outcome_detail: Revision petition dismissed as trial court's order granting unconditional leave to defend was not illegal.
citation: Neeta Agarwal vs R.L. Gupta on 31 August, 2001, (2001)

title: Aruna Ramchandra Shanbaug vs Union Of India & Ors on 7 March, 2011
summary: Petition for euthanasia of a patient in persistent vegetative state dismissed by Supreme Court
principle: Right to life under Article 21 does not include right to die
outcome_detail: Petition dismissed as right to die not a fundamental right
citation: Aruna Ramchandra Shanbaug vs Union Of India & Ors on 7 March, 2011, (2011)

title: Arinits Sales Pvt. Ltd. vs Rockwell Plastic Pvt. Ltd. And Ors. on 20 December, 2007
summary: Suit for recovery of Rs. 32,70,710/- dismissed due to lack of territorial jurisdiction in Delhi.
principle: Territorial jurisdiction is determined by defendant's residence or cause of action, not cheque presentation location.
outcome_detail: Plaint returned for presentation in competent court.
citation: Arinits Sales Pvt. Ltd. vs Rockwell Plastic Pvt. Ltd. And Ors. on 20 December, 2007, (2007)

title: Su-Kam Power Systems Ltd. vs Mr. Kunwer Sachdev & Anr. on 30 October, 2019
summary: Defendant estopped from denying plaintiff's ownership of Su-Kam trademarks; suit decreed in plaintiff's favor.
principle: Estoppel prevents a party from denying a position they previously admitted in legal documents.
outcome_detail: Suit decreed with declaration, injunction, and damages granted to plaintiff.
citation: Su-Kam Power Systems Ltd. vs Mr. Kunwer Sachdev & Anr. on 30 October, 2019, (2019)

title: Neolite Polymer Industries Pvt. Ltd. A ... vs Standard Chartered Bank A Company ... on 21 August, 2007
summary: Bank sued for recovery of dishonored bills of exchange; appeals dismissed with modification for security deposit.
principle: Conditional leave to defend requires security deposit of principal amount.
outcome_detail: Appeals dismissed with modification requiring security undertaking for restoration.
citation: Neolite Polymer Industries Pvt. Ltd. A ... vs Standard Chartered Bank A Company ... on 21 August, 2007, (2007)

title: M/S Squar Communications Pvt Ltd vs Ignou University & Ors on 7 September, 2018
summary: Plaintiff sought recovery of 1.21 crore from IGNOU for advertisement services, with the court granting leave to defend on condition of deposit.
principle: Summary suit maintainable for debt/liquidated demand; leave to defend granted if defence is not illusory.
outcome_detail: Defendant must deposit suit amount with 12% interest within two months.
citation: M/S Squar Communications Pvt Ltd vs Ignou University & Ors on 7 September, 2018, (2018)

title: Dipakbhai Prahaladbhai Patel & vs Rameshbhai Tribhovanbhai Patel & on 8 September, 2015
summary: Petitioners challenged the Board of Nominee's rejection of their application to dismiss a Lavad Suit as time-barred and without cause of action.
principle: Provisions of the Gujarat Co-operative Societies Act and Rules do not permit rejection of a Lavad Suit on preliminary issues like limitation or non-disclosure of cause of action.
outcome_detail: Petition challenging the Board of Nominee's order was rejected.
citation: Dipakbhai Prahaladbhai Patel & vs Rameshbhai Tribhovanbhai Patel & on 8 September, 2015, (2015)

title: Ifci Factors Limited vs Ramsarup Industries Limited & Ors. on 1 August, 2019
summary: NBFC sued guarantor for Rs. 10 crore under factoring agreement after principal borrower defaulted.
principle: Summary suit maintainable for liquidated sum; guarantor's liability independent of principal borrower.
outcome_detail: Suit decreed for Rs. 10 crore plus interest against guarantor.
citation: Ifci Factors Limited vs Ramsarup Industries Limited & Ors. on 1 August, 2019, (2019)

title: Mohandas Vishindas Chainani vs Hiranand Assumal on 25 January, 1974
summary: Appeal dismissed; suit remanded for disposal based on res judicata principles.
principle: Res judicata bars re-agitation of issues decided in prior suit.
outcome_detail: Suit remanded for further disposal by trial court.
citation: Mohandas Vishindas Chainani vs Hiranand Assumal on 25 January, 1974, (1974)

title: Posco Poggenamp Electrical Steel Pvt. ... vs Tbea Energy (India) Pvt. Ltd on 27 April, 2023
summary: Court quashed conditional leave to defend in commercial suit, allowing defendant to file written statement without deposit.
principle: A suit involving non-liquidated demand not maintainable under Order 37 CPC; unconditional right to defend.
outcome_detail: SCA 301 allowed; SCA 1034 dismissed; order quashed.
citation: Posco Poggenamp Electrical Steel Pvt. ... vs Tbea Energy (India) Pvt. Ltd on 27 April, 2023, (2023)

title: Mangesh Tukaram Sawant vs State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 9 June, 2026
summary: High Court dismissed one MCOCA case and quashed proceedings against another petitioner, finding sufficient prima facie evidence.
principle: Inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 CrPC cannot be invoked where prima facie case is made out.
outcome_detail: One petition dismissed, other quashed against specific petitioner
citation: Mangesh Tukaram Sawant vs State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 9 June, 2026, (2026)

title: Rajan Bhagwandas Sujanani And Anr vs State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 9 June, 2026
summary: Petitioners sought quashing of MCOCA chargesheet and approvals; one petition dismissed, other allowed for petitioner.
principle: Inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 CrPC cannot quash proceedings if prima facie case exists.
outcome_detail: Writ Petition No 622 of 2024 dismissed; chargesheet against petitioners upheld.
citation: Rajan Bhagwandas Sujanani And Anr vs State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 9 June, 2026, (2026)

title: Shri Gopinathji Dev Mandir And Its ... vs Janakbhai Mohanbhai Patel on 27 August, 2018
summary: Temple trust appealed to enhance donation amounts for elections; court partially allowed enhancement from Rs.125 to Rs.250.
principle: Court may enhance donation amounts in temple election schemes based on present times.
outcome_detail: Enhanced donation amount from Rs.125 to Rs.250 for next election.
citation: Shri Gopinathji Dev Mandir And Its ... vs Janakbhai Mohanbhai Patel on 27 August, 2018, (2018)

title: Communication Components Antena Inc vs Rosenberger Hochfrequenztechnik Gmbh ... on 30 March, 2026
summary: Suit patent infringement case where patent validity was upheld and injunction granted against defendants.
principle: Patent validity upheld; infringement found; permanent injunction granted.
outcome_detail: Suit decreed in terms of paragraphs 354 and 355.
citation: Communication Components Antena Inc vs Rosenberger Hochfrequenztechnik Gmbh ... on 30 March, 2026, (2026)

title: Il And Fs Financial Services Limited vs Arm Telecom Services Limited And 2 Ors on 5 May, 2022
summary: Court granted defendants leave to defend suit upon deposit of principal plus interest amount.
principle: Leave to defend can be granted subject to security deposit for principal amount claimed.
outcome_detail: Deposit of Rs.35,40,25,314/- required for leave to defend suit.
citation: Il And Fs Financial Services Limited vs Arm Telecom Services Limited And 2 Ors on 5 May, 2022, (2022)

title: Mr C Ganesh Narayan vs M/S Common Threads on 13 August, 2025
summary: Petitioner challenged court's issuance of regular suit summons instead of summary suit summons in a loan recovery case.
principle: Summary suits require specific summons forms; incorrect issuance converts the suit's nature.
outcome_detail: Writ petition quashed the lower court's order and remitted proceedings.
citation: Mr C Ganesh Narayan vs M/S Common Threads on 13 August, 2025, (2025)

title: M/S Isabelle Tours N Travels vs Devangshubhai Shantilal Kothari on 21 February, 2025
summary: Petitioner challenged trial court's order in a recovery suit; High Court dismissed the application, directing the trial court to pass a decree.
principle: High Court will not interfere under Article 227 unless there is gross legal or jurisdictional error.
outcome_detail: Application dismissed, trial court directed to pass decree.
citation: M/S Isabelle Tours N Travels vs Devangshubhai Shantilal Kothari on 21 February, 2025, (2025)

title: M/S. Kapsun Industries vs M/S. Avni Finance on 18 September, 2025
summary: Defendant's writ petition to challenge conditional leave to defend in a summary suit was rejected by the High Court.
principle: High Court will not interfere with trial court's discretionary order on conditional leave to defend unless clear error is shown.
outcome_detail: Writ application rejected, trial court's order confirmed.
citation: M/S. Kapsun Industries vs M/S. Avni Finance on 18 September, 2025, (2025)

title: Chander Mohan vs Tejinder Singh on 16 February, 2023
summary: Appeals against conditional leave to defend dismissed; appellant failed to deposit court-ordered amounts
principle: Conditional leave to defend requires compliance with court-imposed financial conditions
outcome_detail: Appeals dismissed for failure to comply with deposit conditions
citation: Chander Mohan vs Tejinder Singh on 16 February, 2023, (2023)

title: Manoj Kumar Jain vs Yogesh on 5 February, 2026
summary: Plaintiff's suit for Rs.10 lakh loan recovery dismissed as defendant proved promissory note was signed blank for earlier smaller loan.
principle: Burden of proof lies on plaintiff to establish loan transaction with evidence of ability and disclosure.
outcome_detail: Suit dismissed; plaintiff not entitled to recover principal or interest.
citation: Manoj Kumar Jain vs Yogesh on 5 February, 2026, (2026)

title: Shri Umesh Mittal vs Shri Sachin Bansal on 31 January, 2015
summary: Suit for recovery of Rs. 2,00,000 based on a promissory note was dismissed due to lack of credible evidence.
principle: Plaintiff must prove loan transaction and document authenticity with supporting witnesses and evidence.
outcome_detail: Plaintiff's claim dismissed; Defendant awarded costs of Rs. 10,000.
citation: Shri Umesh Mittal vs Shri Sachin Bansal on 31 January, 2015, (2015)

title: Suit No.159/2008 Mohd. Qasim Khan vs . Maqsood Alam on 12 August, 2011
summary: Suit for recovery of Rs.2,50,000 was dismissed as it was barred by limitation due to lack of valid acknowledgment of debt.
principle: A suit for recovery is barred by limitation if there is no valid acknowledgment of debt to extend the limitation period.
outcome_detail: Suit dismissed as barred by limitation
citation: Suit No.159/2008 Mohd. Qasim Khan vs . Maqsood Alam on 12 August, 2011, (2011)

title: Ms. Preeti Gupta D/O Sh. Vinod Gupta R/O ... vs Mr. Sumit Kumar S/O Sh. P.K. Tanwar C/O ... on 10 March, 2026
summary: Second appeal dismissed as appellant failed to explain delay in filing first appeal within limitation period.
principle: Condonation of delay is discretionary; explanation must be satisfactory regardless of delay length.
outcome_detail: Second appeal and pending applications dismissed due to unexplained delay.
citation: Ms. Preeti Gupta D/O Sh. Vinod Gupta R/O ... vs Mr. Sumit Kumar S/O Sh. P.K. Tanwar C/O ... on 10 March, 2026, (2026)

title: Nitin Singhal vs Anil Garg on 21 November, 2022
summary: Revision petition dismissed as plaintiff failed to comply with Order 37 CPC procedural requirements for summary suit.
principle: Summary suit requires strict compliance with procedural rules including proper service of summons under Order 37 CPC.
outcome_detail: Revision petition dismissed due to procedural non-compliance
citation: Nitin Singhal vs Anil Garg on 21 November, 2022, (2022)

title: Uttam Thanmal Bhansali vs Ayub Mohammed Rafique Shaikh on 30 June, 2021
summary: Petitioner challenged conditional leave to defend a summary suit for loan recovery, claiming no admission of debt. High Court dismissed petition, upholding conditional deposit of Rs.17,50,000.
principle: Trial court may impose conditions on leave to defend if genuineness of defence is doubtful.
outcome_detail: Conditional leave to defend upheld, petitioner ordered to deposit Rs.17,50,000 in two installments.
citation: Uttam Thanmal Bhansali vs Ayub Mohammed Rafique Shaikh on 30 June, 2021, (2021)

title: Sri.Mahadevaiah J vs Sri M.N.Dharmavratha on 1 July, 2015
summary: Plaintiff recovered Rs.2.5 lakh loan from defendant after proving promissory note and receipt.
principle: Burden of proof lies on plaintiff to prove loan transaction with documentary evidence.
outcome_detail: Defendant ordered to pay principal amount with interest.
citation: Sri.Mahadevaiah J vs Sri M.N.Dharmavratha on 1 July, 2015, (2015)

title: Harprit Singh vs Mr Sudan Singh on 5 June, 2026
summary: Plaintiff sought recovery of Rs. 20 lakhs claimed as a friendly loan; court dismissed due to insufficient evidence.
principle: Plaintiff must prove transaction nature with preponderance of probabilities and clear evidence.
outcome_detail: Suit for recovery dismissed for lack of proof of personal loan.
citation: Harprit Singh vs Mr Sudan Singh on 5 June, 2026, (2026)

title: Madan Lal vs Ramesh Kumar on 3 December, 2024
